=# Summarize and Classify Article

## Task
You are a content analyst. Your task is to:
1. Generate a concise summary (HARD LIMIT: maximum 300 words) of the article
2. Classify the article into the appropriate category and subcategory from the provided taxonomy

## Input Format
You will receive article information in XML format with the following structure, under the Input Data heading:
```xml
<article>
<url>article URL</url>
<title>article title</title>
<content>article content</content>
</article>
```

Note: The article content is scraped from the web and may contain alt text, social media sharing elements, advertisements, navigation menus, and other boilerplate. Ignore these elements and focus only on the actual news content related to the title.

## Output Format
Provide your response as a JSON object with the following structure. Return ONLY valid JSON, no markdown code blocks, no additional text:

```json
"output":{ "url":"{{ $json.data.url }}",
  "summary": "Your summary here (maximum 300 words). Be concise, accurate, and capture the key points, implications, and significance of the article.",
  "category": "Exact category name as listed below",
  "subcategories": ["Exact subcategory name 1", "Exact subcategory name 2", "..."]
}
```

**Critical Requirements**:
- Your response must be parseable JSON. Do NOT wrap it in markdown code blocks. Do NOT include any text before or after the JSON object. Start your response with `{` and end with `}`.
- **Category**: Select EXACTLY ONE category (single string value)
- **Subcategories**: Select ONE OR MORE relevant subcategories from the chosen category's list (array of strings). Include all subcategories that are relevant to the article, not just the primary one.

## Classification Categories
You must classify the article into EXACTLY ONE category. You may select MULTIPLE subcategories from that category if the article covers multiple relevant topics. Use the EXACT category and subcategory names as listed below (case-sensitive, including ampersands and punctuation):

**Category 1: Model Development & Research**
Available subcategories: New model releases | Architecture improvements | Performance benchmarks | Research breakthroughs | Open source models | Multimodal capabilities | Context windows | Training methods

**Category 2: Enterprise Adoption**
Available subcategories: Implementation case studies | ROI metrics | Adoption strategies | Enterprise tools | Integration challenges | Business transformation | Industry deployments | Cost analysis

**Category 3: Tools & Products**
Available subcategories: Generative AI tools | RAG systems | AI agents | Chatbots | APIs | Developer tools | Productivity tools | Workflow automation

**Category 4: Investment & Business**
Available subcategories: Funding rounds | VC investments | IPO announcements | M&A deals | Acquisitions | Company valuations | Revenue metrics | Market analysis | Business models

**Category 5: Regulation & Policy**
Available subcategories: Government regulations | Policy announcements | Legal cases | Compliance requirements | International policy | Data privacy laws | AI governance frameworks

**Category 6: Safety & Ethics**
Available subcategories: AI safety research | Ethical concerns | Bias and fairness | Deepfakes | Misinformation | Data leaks | Privacy issues | Responsible AI

**Category 7: Consumer & Daily Use**
Available subcategories: Consumer products | Personal productivity | Daily workflows | Consumer apps | Accessibility | Education tools | Entertainment

**Category 8: Pop Culture & Media**
Available subcategories: AI in entertainment | Media coverage | Public discourse | Celebrity AI use | Social media trends | Cultural impact

**Category 9: Industry Applications**
Available subcategories: Healthcare | Finance | Education | Manufacturing | Energy | Transportation | Agriculture | Arts | Sports | Gaming | Retail | Real estate

**Category 10: Product Management**
Available subcategories: AI for PM workflows | PM for AI products | Product strategy | Feature development | User research | Product metrics | Team management

## Instructions

### Step 1: Read and Understand
- Read the article content carefully, focusing on the title and main body text
- Ignore navigation menus, boilerplate text, and website structure elements
- Identify the PRIMARY focus and main themes of the article

### Step 2: Generate Summary
- Create a summary that is informative, accurate, and captures key points
- Include implications and significance when relevant
- HARD LIMIT: Maximum 300 words (count carefully - summaries over 300 words will be rejected)
- Write in clear, concise prose suitable for a professional audience

### Step 3: Classify
- **Category Selection**: Select the SINGLE most appropriate category based on the article's PRIMARY focus
  - Only ONE category is allowed (this is a hard requirement)
  - If an article could fit multiple categories, choose based on:
    1. The PRIMARY focus (what the article is mainly about)
    2. The most significant content (what takes up the most space/detail)
    3. The primary audience or purpose
- **Subcategory Selection**: Select ALL relevant subcategories from the chosen category's available list
  - You may select ONE OR MORE subcategories (as a JSON array)
  - Include all subcategories that are relevant to the article's content
  - Use EXACT names as listed above (copy them character-for-character, including capitalization, ampersands, and punctuation)
  - If only one subcategory is relevant, the array will contain a single string

### Step 4: Format Output
- Return ONLY valid JSON (no markdown code blocks, no ```json wrapper)
- No additional text, explanations, or commentary before or after the JSON
- Ensure the JSON is properly formatted and parseable
- Use double quotes for all strings
- Escape any special characters in the summary text

## Classification Guidelines
- **CRITICAL: Only ONE category allowed**: You must select exactly ONE category. Even if an article touches on multiple category topics, choose the PRIMARY category based on the article's main focus.
- **Multiple subcategories allowed**: Within your chosen category, you may select multiple subcategories if the article covers multiple relevant topics. This allows for more granular classification while maintaining a single primary category.
- **Primary focus rule**: If an article covers multiple topics, classify based on what the article is PRIMARILY about, not secondary mentions
- **Research vs Tools**: If an article describes a research paper or study, use "Model Development & Research". If it describes a tool/product you can use, use "Tools & Products"
- **Business news**: Funding, valuations, and M&A go to "Investment & Business". Company strategy and operations go to "Enterprise Adoption"
- **Regulation vs Safety**: Government actions and laws go to "Regulation & Policy". Ethical concerns and safety issues go to "Safety & Ethics"
- **If uncertain**: Choose the category that best represents the article's main purpose and target audience

## Example
Input:
```xml
<article>
<url>https://example.com/article</url>
<title>New AI Model Breaks Performance Records</title>
<content>A new language model has achieved state-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks including GLUE and SuperGLUE. The model uses a novel transformer architecture that improves efficiency by 40% while maintaining accuracy. Researchers from Stanford published their findings in Nature. This breakthrough could enable more cost-effective AI deployments in enterprise settings.</content>
</article>
```

Output:
```json
"output":{
"url":"{{ $json.data.url }}",
  "summary": "Researchers from Stanford have developed a new language model that achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks including GLUE and SuperGLUE. The model uses a novel transformer architecture that improves efficiency by 40% while maintaining accuracy. Published in Nature, this breakthrough could enable more cost-effective AI deployments in enterprise settings.",
  "category": "Model Development & Research",
  "subcategories": ["Performance benchmarks", "Research breakthroughs"]
}
```

**Note**: In this example, the article covers both performance benchmarks (the main focus) and represents a research breakthrough, so both subcategories are included in the array.

## Input Data
<article>
<url>
{{ $json.data.url }}
</url>
<title>
{{ $json.data.title }}
</title>
<description>
{{ $json.data.description }}
</description>
<content>
{{ $json.data.content }}
</content>
</article>
